THE FIN. Where the dark crest stands now, between the two horns at the crown of the head, stands an orca's dorsal fin: the fin Flux has in picture 2. It is one tall, smooth blade of wet black skin with no hair on it, broad where it grows from the crown, narrowing as it rises and hooked a little back at its tip, half as high as the horns, with one hard line of light down its leading edge. THE SKIN BEHIND THE FACE. Behind the face Flux is an orca. From the temples back the fur ends and the head is smooth, wet, hairless black skin, as glossy as the fin, with long soft highlights from the glass: the temples, the back of the head, the nape and the sides of the neck down into the collar. On that black skin, just behind and above each eye, lies one crisp white oval patch with a clean edge, an orca's own eye patch, twice as long as the eye and swept back toward the ear. OUTSIDE THE GLASS. Two thick glowing rings, pale blue-white, stand in the dark behind, already passed, and far back a jade teal ribbon and a ruby magenta ribbon of such bricks curve toward them, each led by a small bright craft. Beside the course drifts a coral of indigo and violet bricks set edge to edge in rings round open holes, with a spray of white needles in every hole, and a few pale lilac crystals shaped like twelve-sided dice hang in the dark. All of it is inside the ball, and the ball touches nothing. It shows that same course, whole and small: a line of the pale rings set one beyond another like hoops, three tiny bright craft threading them, and behind each craft its long curving ribbon of tiny bricks, one amber gold, one jade teal, one ruby magenta, with the coral beside the course, the crystals along the racing line and the net of six-sided panes curving behind it all.
